what: Marathon Petroleum refines crude oil into petrol, diesel and jet fuel, with about three million barrels a day of capacity, and distributes those fuels. It also controls MPLX, a large pipeline and natural gas processing business.
customers: Fuel wholesalers, retailers and commercial buyers; midstream customers shipping crude and gas.
money: converting crude into fuels and selling them wholesale
moat: Refineries that are effectively impossible to build new in the United States, plus the scale of its terminal and barge network.
risks: Profit depends on refining margins, which swing violently and are outside its control
Fuel demand faces long-term pressure from electric vehicles
Refineries require heavy maintenance and unplanned outages are costly
opportunities: Midstream earnings from MPLX are contracted and far steadier than refining
It has returned very large amounts of cash through buybacks, shrinking the share count sharply
Limited new refining capacity worldwide supports margins when demand is firm
watch: Refining margin per barrel by region and the pace of share repurchases.
